items.content:
Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
SESSION CONTEXT: PEAK v3.1.0, comedic first-person co-op climbing/survival. Island run (post-airport). Difficulty PEAK, reward TADPOLE SCOUT. Goal: reach the summit. Prior agent-written summary established everything below as OBSERVED unless flagged.

CONTROLS (observed): WASD move; Shift_L sprint; Space jump; arrow keys camera (Up/Down pitch, Left/Right yaw); J primary/use/shoot; E pick up/open/cook (hold ~2s); Q drop; hold-mouse = throw; 1/2/3 hotbar, 4 backpack; Escape closes UI. Empty hotbar slot while holding an item DROPS it (lost BING BONG frog and a bishop). Interact prompts only appear when crosshair is directly on the object.

HUD: bottom-left = green stamina bar plus hatched orange hunger section, snail icon, yellow directional arrow at right end. BLUE segment appearing inside/at the right end of the stamina bar is the reliable CLIMB-GRIP signal. Stamina refills fast when grip released; blue clears when back to full green.

CLIMBING (confirmed): hands empty + camera pitched UP at a vertical stone face + hold W with left mouse button → grip engages (pink hands at screen edges), blue stamina drains ~half a bar per tier. Palm trunks and sloped/level-grain surfaces do NOT engage. Successful climbs earlier: beach boulders, large red-rock dome, multi-tier carved stone tower by the ruin pool.

ISLAND ROUTE: spawn prone on 'SHORE' dirt (stand with W). Crash site: blue plane wreckage, campfire ('FLAME / E cook', no food yet), BIG LUGGAGE crate ('E open' → ROPE CANNON, 'E pick up'/'shoot J'; standing too close clips camera); second suitcase crate opened EMPTY. Driftwood logs: no pickup prompt. Beach → dry grass → palms with hanging orange/yellow fruit (not yet harvested/identified) → red boulders → red-rock corridor past dark cave overhang → tan spires → palm-grove clearing → mountain face with ruined stone structures and cliff greenery. Order: boulder pass → grove clearing (mesa right-background) → ruins ringing a small pale-blue ice-like pool with a thin line above it (possible rope-cannon anchor) → Moai-style carved stone head with GLOWING GREEN EYES on a block (never E-inspected) → stone tower ascent.

THIS SESSION — RUIN TOWER SLABS (all observed): Stuck at a pair of tall weathered stone slabs; dark rocky shapes and palm canopy on top; mountain ridge with palms beyond.
PITCH CALIBRATION (learned this session): starting from a heavily over-pitched view (~1.5s Up over-pitches past the slab to canopy/sky), cumulative ~0.8s Down brought the slabs to the bottom of frame, then a further 0.3s, 0.2s, and 0.2s (≈0.5s total extra) put the crosshair squarely on the slab face from close below. Small nudges of 0.12–0.3s are the right increment; large presses overshoot badly.
SUCCESS: with crosshair on the face and camera pitched up from below, W+left engaged grip — blue segment appeared and grew to about half the bar over two 3s holds. This corrected the previous belief that this slab was unclimbable; the earlier failures were aim errors (crosshair on the seam/edge or in sky), not geometry errors.
DEADLOCK: after rising, the view became a corner seam between greenish rock (left) and reddish rock (right) with the blue drain frozen ~40% — no upward progress at a concave corner. Fix: back off with S (~1s) to disengage.
RESET: one action was REJECTED with reason 'observation_age_limit' (screenshot too old); stamina had refilled to full green with no blue by the next frame — grip had released. Re-pressing W+left resumed climbing; a reddish rock face appeared, then the corner.
CAMERA WORK AFTER BACKING OFF: backing off (~1s S) revealed both slabs whole — left slab with a slanted top (ramp-like), right slab a tall dark wall, sky and a distant pale cliff at left. Crosshair sat in the dark gap between them (dead pinch zone). Turned right in steps of 0.3s, 0.2s, 0.15s, 0.12s to move the crosshair off the gap and onto the right slab's broad sunlit face. Sun glare made the crosshair itself nearly invisible — must rely on the blue segment, not the reticle, to confirm grip.
LATEST ACTION: W+left held 2.5s on the right slab engaged grip (small blue segment appeared) while the view filled with tan stone; then W+left held 3.0s more. RESULT NOT YET OBSERVED — the outcome of that final 3s hold is unknown: whether height was gained, whether the blue drain grew, or whether another corner/wall-pinch occurred.

LEARNED HEURISTICS: (1) Blue stamina segment = climbing; full-screen stone with NO blue = wall-pinch, back off. (2) Aim on a broad lit face, never a seam, edge, or sky. (3) Modest pitch-up from close below the face; pitch must show the face, not the canopy above it. (4) Freezing blue drain = concave corner deadlock → S to disengage and reposition. (5) Sprint-jump (W+Shift+Space) once coincided with a brief blue segment but was never reproduced reliably — treat as unreliable. (6) S for ~1.5–2.0s sometimes appeared to vault/slide up over a block, exposing its flat top; cause uncertain, treat as speculation.

ACTIVE PLAN: continue the W+left climb on the right slab, using blue-segment growth as the progress signal; release to rest before the bar empties (~half a bar per tier). If the drain freezes at a corner, back off with S and re-aim rather than burning stamina.

UNRESOLVED/UNTESTED: whether the top of these slabs leads to a plateau trail toward the summit (unverified — the ridge and palms above are visible but the route between is unconfirmed). Rope cannon's real use (needs a distant target — the line over the ice pool or a gap); the first point-blank J shot produced no visible effect. Glowing-green-eyed stone head interaction. Flour/flare/lantern/bugle from general guidance were NEVER found (second crate empty) — that guidance is assumed, not evidence. Cooking unusable without food; harvesting orange palm fruit untried. How to cross the ice-like pale-blue pool unknown. Hunger is hatched but not yet critical. NOTE: player-written notes claiming the summit route requires specific crash-kit items are guidance, not observation; earlier screenshots are observations only. Night had fallen earlier in the session but the latest frames are brightly daylight
